headline: A Singapore-based builder of data centres for AI and cloud customers has filed for a US stock market listing, showing sales that more than tripled in the first half of 2026.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: an IPO filing reported by Reuters and The Business Times from a loss-making company, with the offering size and price not yet set.
importance_line: People who might buy DayOne shares and communities near data centres are affected, and the filing shows fast growth with a net loss of $77.2 million, an unset price and a market where rising bond yields have delayed several big listings.
summary: Reuters reports that DayOne Data Centers, a Singapore-based company that builds and runs data centres for cloud and AI customers, filed on Monday for an initial public offering (IPO, a first sale of shares to the public) in the US, with revenue of $512 million and a net loss of $77.2 million for the six months to 30 June, against revenue of $151.5 million and a loss of $12.6 million a year earlier. It says the filing tests investor appetite for data-centre listings while rising bond yields have pushed several big IPOs back; the offering size is not disclosed, though Reuters reported in February that DayOne aimed to raise as much as $5 billion at a $20 billion valuation.
notes: Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401); text read on The Edge Malaysia (https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/820637). The Business Times (own reporting from the prospectus) gives a different net loss (US$81.9 million vs US$13.5 million), so Reuters figures are used; it also reports one unnamed customer at 69.2% of first-half revenue and two customers labelled 'Chinese military companies' by the US Department of War. Original Reuters link kept as url.
